transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-06-21 15:00 UTC | Duration: 46m | Attendees: Maya Chen, Ravi Patel (Redwood) — Lisa Monroe, Jonas Kim, Priya Singh, Michael Torres (Crestline)

Summary: quick weekly POC sync focused on an access snag: staging nodes couldn't reach Redwood gateway from their VPC; discussed short-term mitigation, SSO/KMS integration blockers, and plan for canary fallback to hosted variant. Agreed next steps and owners.

Topics: onboarding progress; VPC egress / firewall rules; SSO/SAML and KMS handoff; benchmark re-run; rollback/canary fallback strategy; security checklist.

Transcript: 
[00:00] Maya: okay hi everyone, thanks for joining, this is the weekly POC sync for Crestline, uh we'll run about 45 minutes, quick agenda — access update, security handoffs, bench results and then next steps. 
[00:25] Lisa: thanks Maya, quick heads up we hit a blocker this morning, our staging cluster can't reach the redwood gateway, we saw TCP reset on egress, so the pilot's paused.
[00:35] Jonas: yeah the egress went through our transit VPC but looks like the firewall is dropping the connection to the 52.XX.XX.XX range, I have a ticket with infra but I wanted to align on mitigations.
[00:50] Ravi: okay can you paste the traceroute and the port 443 check? often it's just an IP allowlist on the provider side or an intermediate NGFW killing TLS SNI.
[01:05] Jonas: sending the trace in the chat now, looks like a reset after hop 5, we haven't configured the static NAT for the peering.
[01:20] Priya: just to add security context, we need audit log visibility and KMS integration before we can accept the private deploy. For the immediate short term, does Redwood support a hosted fallback while we finish KMS?
[01:35] Maya: yes, we can route traffic to our hosted endpoint as a temporary fallback, it will have different data handling — we need a paperwork signoff and we can spin up sandbox creds. we'll note the data residency caveats.
[01:50] Michael: what does 'different handling' mean for PHI? we are in health vertical so we need clarity.
[01:58] Maya: good question, hosted endpoints are isolated but not under your customer-managed KMS; for PHI we recommend Dedicated or Private with customer KMS, hosted is only for metadata-free, limited testing — Ravi can go into the tradeoffs.
[02:12] Ravi: yeah hosted will still encrypt at rest, but keys are managed by Redwood's KMS; we offer BYOK on Private which plugs into your AWS KMS and HSM backed flows. For the pilot we can use hosted for functional tests and switch to Private/Dedicated for production.
[02:30] Lisa: okay that helps. Jonas, can you try the allowlist step so we can unblock staging?
[02:36] Jonas: will do, but the firewall team needs the IPs and the HA pairs, also the peering config.
[02:42] Maya: I'll email the allowlist IPs and the subnet ranges right after this call, plus the sandbox creds.
[02:50] Priya: also we need SAML metadata and SSO certs — is Redwood able to do IdP-initiated SSO for the console?
[03:00] Maya: yes we support SAML 2.0, SP-initiated and IdP-initiated, and we can share the ACS URL and metadata; SE will help with the assertion consumer URL mapping.
[03:12] Ravi: one caveat we ran into with another customer, sometimes attribute mapping (like groups -> RBAC roles) needs a small script on the IdP to get the group name formatting right, so plan for 1-2 small iterations.
[03:28] Lisa: got it. switching gears — bench results. we re-ran the 1k prompt test yesterday after the initial warmups, numbers are here: average p95 latency 420ms on 16k context, the redwood numbers earlier were quoted at ~310ms; any idea why the delta?
[03:48] Ravi: couple possibilities — your tokenization pattern and prompt prefixing, plus the staging nodes had KV cache cold starts after the restart, also we saw CPU steal on the instance during the run. did you run with prefix caching enabled?
[04:02] Michael: we used the sample app config, I think caching wasn't enabled because of the restart.
[04:08] Ravi: that'd do it, cold KV cache can add 80-130ms to p95 depending on sequence length. we can re-run with cache warm and a higher concurrent QPS to match the redwood bench harness.
[04:20] Jonas: question — does Redwood's runtime do dynamic batching on the hosted path too? we saw some throughput but not sure about latency SLOs.
[04:28] Ravi: yes, dynamic batching is enabled across the runtime, but the batch size and timeout heuristics vary by deployment mode. Dedicated has tighter SLOs because we tune batch windows for lower latency.
[04:38] Priya: from compliance side, can we see request-level audit logs, including user-id and model-version?
[04:45] Maya: yes we provide per-request trace with model id, token counts, and request metadata in the audit log. for Private we can push audit logs to your CloudWatch/Stackdriver or S3.
[04:56] Lisa: great. follow-up on KMS — Jonas, you said AWS KMS, do we need any specific grants?
[05:03] Jonas: yes we need to create a grant for the Redwood service principal, and we also can't allow key deletion, so it's a narrow grant.
[05:12] Ravi: we'll send a template policy for the KMS grants.
[05:16] Maya: action: we'll share the KMS grant template and SAML metadata after the call.
[05:22] Jonas: thanks. back to the access snag — if we can't get allowlist in time, can we use a temporary SSH tunnel?
[05:30] Ravi: technically yes but that's operationally heavy and brittle; hosted fallback is cleaner for a few days while infra sorts the peering.
[05:38] Michael: how will billing work if we go hosted temporarily? we don't want to be charged production rates.
[05:44] Maya: we can set the pilot billing to a sandbox tier and cap spend; I'll add that to the note when I send creds.
[05:51] Lisa: perfect.
[05:55] [09:12] Jonas: i'm pasting the firewall ticket link now — it shows the NGFW blocked due to SNI mismatch, apparently the proxy rewrote TLS SNI and reset.
[09:22] Maya: okay that explains it, NGFW rewriting SNI is common in older stacks, we can provide a TLS fingerprint and hostname to match, but sometimes you need the allowlist at the provider layer instead of proxy.
[09:34] Priya: on the security checklist, can Redwood provide SOC2 type II attestation and a signed subprocessors list?
[09:42] Maya: yes we have SOC2 II report and subprocessors PDF, I'll attach the redacted report, SE will send subprocessors list.
[09:50] Ravi: adding a note — for the Private deployment the subprocessors are mostly infra partners, we can also support contractual restrictions for certain data types.
[09:58] Lisa: excellent. 
[10:05] Michael: small product question — how do model rollouts look? we want canary 10% traffic then 50% then full if metrics good.
[10:13] Ravi: that's built-in: we support canary/A-B by traffic percents, metrics gating on latency, error rate, and eval sets. we can also set automatic fallback to previous model if data quality drops.
[10:25] Lisa: will that preserve KV cache across rollbacks?
[10:30] Ravi: cache continuity across model variants is tricky, we keep KV cache per model variant; for small model patching we can reuse some cache, but usually we flush on major version changes to avoid token corruption.
[10:42] Lisa: okay noted.
[10:45] Maya: quick check — timeline expectations, are we aiming to go to pilot production by end of July?
[10:52] Michael: still the target but it's contingent on infra unblocking and KMS.
[10:58] Jonas: i think if allowlist and KMS grants are in this week we can keep July target.
[11:05] Priya: security wants a smoke test for PHI handling before prod, that's a two-week window once KMS is live.
[11:12] Maya: understood, we'll factor that in.
[11:18] Lisa: any open engineering risks we haven't covered?
[11:22] Ravi: one more — model quantization profile used in staging was 8-bit; it performed well but we've seen slightly different tokenization leading to hallucinations on a small prompt subset — recommend running a targeted eval set.
[11:36] Lisa: can you run the eval against our privacy-sensitive prompt set? we'll share in the portal.
[11:42] Ravi: yes we'll run it, please mark the prompt set in the shared drive with the tag "PHI-eval".
[11:48] Maya: we'll schedule the eval and share results in the next sync.
[11:52] [20:00] Jonas: quick infra note — provider peering delays happen at scale, i need a fallback policy for traffic egress in our runbook.
[20:08] Maya: we'll provide suggested runbook text for fallback: fallback to hosted endpoint, circuit-breaker, and alerting thresholds. I'll put that in the shared Confluence.
[20:18] Michael: please include cost delta guidance for fallback.
[20:22] Maya: yes.
[20:26] [28:30] Priya: on encryption in-transit, do you support mTLS? we prefer mutual TLS for service-to-service when in private mode.
[28:38] Ravi: yes Private supports mTLS; for hosted we rely on TLS1.3 and application-level auth; mTLS is part of Private deployment checklist.
[28:45] Priya: good.
[28:48] Lisa: we also wanted an emergency rollback play — if latency spikes >500ms p95 for 3 consecutive minutes, automatically route to fallback. Is that supported?
[28:58] Ravi: yes we can wire that up with our Smart Routing policies, with a cooldown and manual override.
[29:06] Lisa: nice.
[29:10] Maya: recap — immediate: Maya sends allowlist IPs, sandbox creds, KMS template, SAML metadata; Jonas to confirm firewall rule application; Ravi to run warm-cache bench and PHI eval; Priya to share SOC2 scope doc.
[29:28] Maya: any other blockers?
[29:30] Jonas: none from infra beyond allowlist.
[29:34] Michael: no.
[29:36] Lisa: nope.
[29:38] Maya: great — i'll follow up with a single email capturing action items, and we'll schedule the KMS deep dive for Thursday.
[29:45] [45:50] End of call.

References shared: pilot-checklist (https://redwood.ai/pilot-checklist), KMS-template (link in follow-up email), firewall ticket (internal link pasted in chat).

Meeting notes (short):
- Root cause: NGFW/proxy rewriting TLS SNI caused connection resets — blocked egress to Redwood gateway IP.
- Short-term mitigation: Hosted fallback + sandbox creds, spend cap.
- Mid-term: Provider-level allowlist + peering adjustment; KMS grant + SAML setup for Private deploy.
- Bench actions: warm KV cache re-run and PHI-targeted eval.

Next sync: scheduled tentatively 2026-06-24 for KMS deep-dive (SE-led).
